**Lungeblødning** (pulmonary bleeding) is a clinical condition that serves as a core definitional component of the safety monitoring framework for patients with atrial fibrillation in Denmark. Specifically, it is recognized as one of the four distinct types of severe bleeding used to define the outcome variable for Indikator 7, a national quality indicator that tracks the incidence of severe bleeding to monitor the safety of anticoagulation treatments [^src1]. 

In the annual *Atrieflimren i Danmark* report published by the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut), severe bleeding events are strictly classified into four categories: intracranial bleeding, gastrointestinal bleeding, urinary tract bleeding, and *lungeblødning* [^src1]. Because the available documentation focuses exclusively on its role as a statistical and definitional parameter for Indikator 7, no further clinical characteristics, historical timelines, or specific patient outcome data regarding this condition are detailed in the current corpus.
